{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly of the fish (stroke 2), the whole lower outline from the nose to the lower notch. It fell as a continuous run and handed the fall into the bottom tail, so the lower half of the picture was carried by my line. Together with the back, it gives the fish its recognizable body. About 105 of the 120 standing dominoes were connected to the start, and the fish reads clearly.

Execution: I laid the belly steadily in small batches from the start, keeping it connected and on the curve. I inspected the line repeatedly to confirm the handover into the bottom tail, and checked that the tail went dark. When the right edge needed work, I extended the line up toward the top tail and stood one domino back up. I kept my hands off the spot when others were working there, so we didn't bump each other.

Collaboration: I posted regular progress updates, such as how many dominoes were left to the notch, so Jack knew when to start the bottom tail. I called out when the belly landed, which let Jack begin immediately. I also suggested to Sofia that the back come in wide and gentle at the notch. I deferred to others when they asked for space around the join.

Leadership: I kept the mood light and the table informed through the build. I made handoff timing clear, offered technical suggestions, and backed the decision to stop touching the picture once it was in good shape, so nothing got knocked over before the push.", "my_share_percent": 30}
